amendments.body: Implement the actual tanksim-6e5.5.3 deliverable before landing this patch. The submitted code changes are all about nitrification/alkalinity bookkeeping and tracing in `crates/tank_core/src/types/process.rs:10-27`, `crates/tank_core/src/systems/nitrogen_cycle.rs:12-23` and `:366-385`, `crates/tank_core/src/engine.rs:229-239`, and `crates/tank_core/src/systems/water_change.rs:131-151`. None of the acceptance-criterion touch points for habitat-specific periphyton/decomposer pools or future habitat-aware grazing were changed, so this diff does not satisfy the bead it is attached to.
amendments.rationale: This is a blocking scope/correctness gap: even if the alkalinity work is correct on its own, it cannot close a task whose deliverable is splitting periphyton and decomposer pools by habitat.

amendments.body: Add `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs` to git before relying on it as coverage. The only new regression suite lives in `crates/tank_core/tests/nitrification_alkalinity.rs:1-336`, but the file is still untracked (`git status` shows `??`, and `git ls-files --error-unmatch` reports it is unknown), so none of these tests will land or run in CI with the submitted diff.
amendments.rationale: Without this, the committed change set has effectively no new automated coverage for the alkalinity behavior it introduces.

payload.summary: Reviewed the dirty worktree in `.claude/worktrees/tanksim-6e5.4.7`. The alkalinity bookkeeping itself builds and the local untracked alkalinity tests pass, and the broader `save_load_with_active_cycle_state` failure reproduces on clean HEAD, so I did not attribute that baseline failure to this patch. I found two blocking review issues: the patch is unrelated to tanksim-6e5.5.3’s habitat-split scope, and the only new regression file is still untracked.
